# Dependencies permitted to run their own install scripts.
#
# `pnpm install` in this repository runs with `--ignore-scripts`, so by default NOTHING a
# dependency ships executes during installation. Review finding [127]: the pre-flight walks the
# manifests in this tree and a dependency's manifest is not in this tree — it arrives inside a
# tarball, is extracted by pnpm, and its `postinstall` ran before any verification in the job. A
# pull request adding a local `.tgz` under `packages/qfai/` and referencing it from the manifest and
# lockfile therefore executed arbitrary code with every guard still ahead of it.
#
# Named here, a dependency is rebuilt explicitly AFTER the install, in a step whose body is pinned
# by `verificationBodies` — and this file's own digest is pinned in the pre-flight step in
# `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. Adding a name is a visible edit to a pinned file, which is the whole
# point: the question stops being "did anyone notice this package runs code" and becomes "did a
# reviewer agree that it may".
#
# Measured rather than guessed. Scanning the installed store for install-time hooks finds 35
# packages, but 34 of them declare only `prepare` — which pnpm runs for git and directory sources
# and NOT for a registry tarball, so none of those ever executed here. `esbuild` is the one with a
# real `postinstall`, and it links the platform binary that vite and vitest need.
#
# One name per line, matched against the package name pnpm knows it by.
esbuild
